subject.title: [Bug]: models.json generator writes apiKey as plain string instead of secret-ref object

question: Should generated provider snapshots retain a non-secret credential marker for compatibility, or should every generated `apiKey` field be omitted after current runtime consumers are verified?
rationale: The recent report indicates a security-sensitive persistence path may remain, but choosing marker-versus-omission semantics requires confirmation of runtime and plugin snapshot consumers and the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Audit all generated snapshot writers
options.body: Recommended: preserve only the established non-secret representation where a verified consumer needs it, otherwise omit `apiKey`, then prove runtime authentication and a clean audit after regeneration.

options.title: Scope to models.json only
options.body: Fix the per-agent models writer first and track catalog snapshot persistence separately if current source confirms distinct ownership and consumers.

options.title: Treat strings as audit-only false positives
options.body: Change scanner classification only if source inspection proves generated values can never be resolved credentials, which the discussion currently does not establish.

recommendation.title: Audit all generated snapshot writers
recommendation.body: Recommended: preserve only the established non-secret representation where a verified consumer needs it, otherwise omit `apiKey`, then prove runtime authentication and a clean audit after regeneration.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier merged change is the clearest available history signal for the generated models credential-redaction boundary.
